title: Three Terms and One Short Mark
subtitle: 学校学习 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 学校学习（人与自我·生活与学习·学校生活与学习）
meta: 主题语境：学校学习（人与自我·生活与学习·学校生活与学习）　|　核心词汇：grade　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 grade 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1969 the teacher ① gave a grade that no parent in the school would have described, and he said the giving was the whole of the term. The ② grade, meaning the mark itself and not the report, ran three terms and stayed undescribed in the book; a grade, he said, is the only thing in a school that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ grade in that school had the same short mark beside it, and the ④ grade at the far board, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A grade, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the teacher said the describing is the part that fills three terms.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the grade was the whole of the matter, meaning the year and not the mark. The ⑥ grade, meaning the year and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; grade, he said, is either something you give or the only word that means both a mark and a year. He said the year is the part they remember.

By 1974 the ⑦ grade had become a line in a card, and the card had become an argument about the short mark. The ⑧ grade of the whole thing, the teacher wrote in November, was one school and three terms of describing; grade, he said, is either the one at the far board or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ grade I remember is the one described in the card, which closed in 1976 and is still described as the quietest in the school. A ⑩ grade, my mother said in 1978, is the only one that improves by being described; every grade, she said, is a year that has agreed to look like a mark. She said the year was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 分数；等级（指学校里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 分数；等级（指那个分数本身，与报告单相对）
C. 固定搭配：give a grade 给一个分数
D. n. 分数（指留给孩子们看的那一个）
E. n. 评分（抽象总称，指一所学校的评分之事）
F. n. 分数（指成绩卡里写到、被记录过的那一个）
G. n. 年级（指一件事里人人都上却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 年级（抽象总称，指人人都上却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: gave a grade that no parent in the school would have described

answers.why: give a grade 意为“给一个分数”，1969 年那位老师给了学校里没有一位家长肯描述的一个分数。
grade 意为“分数、等级”，指那个分数本身而不是报告单，它经过了三个学期而在簿子上没有被描述。
grade 意为“分数、等级”，指学校里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一个矮矮的记号。
grade 意为“分数”，指最远那块板上留给孩子们看的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
grade 意为“年级”，指一件事里人人都上却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个年级就是那件事的全部。
grade 意为“年级”，指人人都上却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个分数，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
grade 意为“分数”，指成绩卡里写到、被记录过的那一个，到 1974 年这一个成了卡上的一行。
grade 意为“评分”，老师十一月写道，整件事的评分之事是一所学校和三个学期的描述。
grade 意为“分数”，我记得的是卡上描述过的那一个，1976 年登记了，至今仍被说成学校里最安静的一个。
grade 为抽象总称，母亲 1978 年说，一个分数是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的东西。
